 ## Unreleased
 
+### Added
+
+Support for authorization servers that are a *dispatching front door*: the
+apex serves `/authorize` and `/device_authorization` but redirects each to a
+regional authorization server, which is the only host that mints tokens and
+the only host that will redeem the resulting code. The client must therefore
+learn the region at runtime and send the token request there.
+
+- `authcode.Flow.Issuer()` — the RFC 9207 `iss` parameter from the loopback
+  callback, or `""` when the server sent none. Reported verbatim and
+  deliberately **not** validated: the package knows the origin it dialled but
+  not the issuer identifier the deployment expects, and for a dispatching
+  front door those legitimately differ (RFC 9207 §2.4 makes validation the
+  client's job). Callers MUST check it against their own trust policy.
+- `authcode.Flow.SetTokenBaseURL(baseURL)` — retargets this flow's token
+  exchange at `baseURL` instead of `Client.BaseURL`. Call it between `Wait`
+  and `Exchange`; `""` clears the override. `baseURL` is validated as an
+  origin (HTTPS unless `AllowInsecureHTTP` and loopback), but the package
+  cannot judge whether the host is trustworthy — the authorization code and
+  the user's tokens travel to it.
+- `deviceflow.DeviceCode.ResponseOrigin` — the origin that actually served
+  the device-authorization response, after any redirects the client followed.
+  Filled in by `StartDeviceAuth`, never decoded from the response body (that
+  body is parsed strictly, so a server-sent field of the same name would be a
+  breaking change). Equals `Client.BaseURL` when no redirect occurred.
+- `deviceflow.Client.TokenBaseURL` — overrides `BaseURL` for the token
+  endpoint only (`PollDeviceAuth` / `PollUntil`). Empty means "use BaseURL".

## Why
https://auth.entire.io (entire-core global mode) will dispatch CLI logins to the caller's regional core: `GET /authorize` 302s the browser to the home/geo region, `POST /device_authorization` 307s by geo. Tokens are minted by the regional core, so the client must exchange/poll against the region — v0.5.2 pinned everything to `Client.BaseURL` and discarded the signals that name the region.

## What
- `authcode`: `Flow.Issuer()` surfaces the RFC 9207 `iss` param from the loopback callback; `Flow.SetTokenBaseURL()` retargets the token exchange per flow.
- `deviceflow`: `DeviceCode.ResponseOrigin` records the origin that served the response after redirects (the 307 target); `Client.TokenBaseURL` overrides the poll endpoint only.
- Neither value is trust-validated here — deliberately the embedder's job (the CLI enforces a strict https-subdomain-of-dialled-host rule).
- Go toolchain bumped 1.26.4 → 1.26.6, clearing the six stdlib advisories govulncheck flagged on the HTTP/TLS paths: GO-2026-6218 (`net/url`), GO-2026-6090 + GO-2026-5856 (`crypto/tls`), GO-2026-6089 + GO-2026-5026 (`net/http`), GO-2026-5972 (`encoding/asn1`). **Raises the `go.mod` minimum — consumers now need Go ≥ 1.26.6.**

## Verification
- `mise run test:ci` (`-race`): all 9 packages pass, incl. new `regional_test.go` in `authcode` and `deviceflow` (httptest apex 307→regional; callback `iss` → retargeted exchange). Coverage 75–95% per package.

**Three conflicts, all in the collision with main's new login UI (#1961):**

1. **`login.go` / `runLogin`** — main moved the `Device code:` print to *after* `chooseApprovalURL`. Kept main's layout and hoisted the issuer-adoption block to immediately after `StartDeviceAuth`, before any output — nothing is shown until the poll target is known.

This one only surfaced under `lint`, not `go build` — `go build ./...` doesn't compile tests. Committed separately as `2abe4944cf`.

**The one thing worth a second look, and it's fine:** main now runs `flow.Wait` on its own goroutine, concurrently with the keypress reader. Our code reads `flow.Issuer()` afterwards, and auth-go documents that field as caller-goroutine-only. Checked every exit path in `waitForLoginURLResult` (`login.go:779-838`) — all six either receive from `waitCh` or receive from it before returning a zero value, so the channel always supplies the happens-before edge. No race, and the issuer is always populated before we read it. Device flow is safe too: `UseTokenIssuer` writes `TokenBaseURL` before the polling goroutine is spawned.

## Why
https://auth.entire.io (entire-core global mode) now dispatches logins to the caller's regional core (https://github.com/entirehq/entiredb/pull/3135): identify-first 302 on `/authorize`, geo 307 on `/device_authorization`. ## What
- `entire login` defaults to `https://auth.entire.io` (`--server` stays for special cases).
- Browser flow reads the RFC 9207 `iss` from the loopback callback and exchanges the code at that regional host; device flow polls the origin that served the 307'd response.
- Token `iss` acceptance: exactly the dialled origin, or a strict https subdomain of it on the same port (`us.auth.entire.io` under `auth.entire.io`; `auth.entire.io.evil.com`, `xauth.entire.io`, scheme/port downgrades all rejected). The mismatch error only offers the subdomain shape when the dialled origin is https, since a plaintext dev/loopback server can never delegate.

## Why
`GET /me`'s `regionalUnavailable` block advertises a profile page that doesn't exist.

Observed live, from an AU-homed account whose device login was geo-routed to EU:

```json
"regionalUnavailable": {
  "error": "foreign_jurisdiction",
  "jurisdiction": "au",
  "homeCoreUrl": "https://au.console.entire.io/#/profile",
  "message": "Your profile is hosted in the au jurisdiction. Open it on au.console.entire.io."
}
```

Opening that URL lands on `/admin.html`. The user-facing console SPA that served `/` was retired (`core/api/server.go:1357`); a bare `/` now runs `handleConsoleRoot` (`core/api/admin_gate.go:144-171`), which redirects purely by role:

| Caller | Lands on |
| --- | --- |
| no session | `/api/auth/login` |
| non-session (api-access) token | marketing site |
| platform admin | `/admin.html` |
| everyone else | marketing site |

So the link resolved to the admin bundle for admins and the **marketing site** for normal users — never a profile. There is nothing to repoint it at either: every other console deep link in this repo is hash-routed under `/admin.html` (`cluster_handlers.go:94`, `admin_mirrors.go:517`), and the admin SPA has no profile route. `identity.go` was the only caller still building the old `base + "/#/profile"` form, and it was never updated when the SPA went away.

## What
- `homeCoreUrl` is now the home console's bare origin — no path, no fragment.
- The message stops instructing the caller to "Open it on `<host>`"; it names where the profile is hosted and identifies the home console.
- The `doc:` tag says the field is an origin, not a deep link, so nobody restores the fragment later.
- Extended the existing foreign-jurisdiction test, which previously asserted only `error`, to pin `jurisdiction`, the fragment-free `homeCoreUrl`, and the absence of the "Open it on" copy.

Deliberately not changing the schema shape: `homeCoreUrl` stays required and populated. Identifying the home console is still useful; promising a page is not.

## Verification
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./core/coreapi/ ./api/corev1/ ./core/api/`, `gofmt -l`: all clean.
- The touched test is DB-backed (`coreapiPool`), so it runs in CI rather than locally.
- No consumers of the old value: `homeCoreUrl` appears in entire.io only in a test fixture (`api/src/lib/entire-core/current-identity.test.ts:300`), entiredb's own SPAs never read it, and the Entire CLI deliberately ignores it — https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1997.

Worth knowing for reviewers: this field is **unrelated** to the 421 redirect envelope's `home_core_url`, which genuinely is an API origin that clients rewrite requests to. Same name, incompatible meanings, two different structs.
